questions.q: Let $A$ and $B$ be two finite sets with $m$ and $n$ elements respectively. The total number of subsets of the set $A$ is $56$ more than the total number of subsets of $B$. Then the distance of the point $P ( m, n )$ from the point $Q ( - 2, - 3 )$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that, the total number of subsets of a set having $n$ elements is ${2}^{n}$.

$⇒ {2}^{m} - {2}^{n} = 56$

$⇒ {2}^{n}\left({2}^{m - n} - 1\right) = {2}^{3} \times 7$

$⇒ {2}^{n} = {2}^{3}$ and ${2}^{m - n} - 1 = 7$

$⇒ n = 3$ and ${2}^{m - n} = 8$

$⇒ n = 3$ and $m - n = 3$

$⇒ n = 3$ and $m = 6$

Distance between $P \left(6, 3\right)$ and $Q \left(-2, - 3\right)$ is given by,

$PQ = \sqrt{\left(6 + 2\right)2 + \left(3 + 3\right)2}$

$⇒ PQ = \sqrt{{8}^{2} + {6}^{2}}$

$⇒ PQ = \sqrt{100}$

$⇒ PQ = 10$ units

Perpendicular bisector of $PR$~is~$2x - y + 2 = 0$~

Midpoint of~$PQ$~is~$M \left(1, 1\right)$

Equation of perpendicular bisector of~$PQ$~is~$y = x$.

Point of intersection of equations~$PR$~and~$PQ$ is circumcentre.

So, circumcentre is~ \left(-2, - 2\right)$

$

questions.q: The distance of the point $( 2, 3 )$ from the line $2x - 3y + 28 = 0$, measured parallel to the line $\sqrt{3}x - y + 1 = 0$, is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, ${L}_{1}: \sqrt{3}x - y + 1 = 0$ and ${L}_{2}: 2x - 3y + 28 = 0$.

Slope, ${m}_{1} = \sqrt{3} = tan\theta$

$⇒ \theta = {60}^{°}$

$⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{2}, cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now, equation of line passing through \left(2, 3\right)$ and having slope $\sqrt{3}$ is,

$\dfrac{x - 2}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{y - 3}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = r$

$⇒ 2x - 3y + 28 = 0$

$⇒ 4 + r - 9 - \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}r + 28 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{2 - 3\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)r + 23 = 0$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{46}{3\sqrt{3} - 2} \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{3} + 2}{3\sqrt{3} + 2}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{46}{23} \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{3} + 2}{1} = 4 + 6\sqrt{3}$

$

questions.q: Let $S$ be the set of all triangles in the $xy$ -plane, each having one vertex at the origin and the other two vertices lie on coordinate axes with integral coordinates. If each triangle in $S$ has area $50$~sq. units, then the number of elements in the set $S$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Since the vertex of given triangle is $O$ (origin) and other two vertices $A$ and $B$ lies on the coordinate axes, hence triangle must be a right-angled triangle.

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}x . y ( x, y \in I )$

As per given condition

$\dfrac{1}{2}x . y = 50 ⇒ x . y = 100$

Possible ordered pairs of \left(x, y\right)$ when $∆$ formed in ${1}^{st}$ quadrant are $9$ i. e. \left(1, 100\right), \left(2, 50\right), \left(4, 25\right), \left(5, 20\right), \left($10, 10\right), \left($25, 4\right), \left($50, 2\right), \left($100, 1\right)$

$∆$ can be formed in any of the quadrants, hence total number of cases $9 \times4 = 36 .$

area~$∆ ABC = $\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\left|\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{13}$ \text{ and } $\dfrac{56}{13}$ \text{ and } 1 \\ $\dfrac{95}{13}$ \text{ and } - $\dfrac{12}{13}$ \text{ and } 1 \\ - $\dfrac{15}{13}$ \text{ and } $\dfrac{32}{13}$ \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right|\right|$

$= $\dfrac{1}{2 \times {13}^{3}}\left||\begin{cases}$3 \text{ and } 56 \text{ and } 13 \\ 95 \text{ and } - 12 \text{ and } 13 \\ - 15 \text{ and } 32 \text{ and } 13\end{cases}\right||$

area~$∆ ABC = $\dfrac{132}{13}sq. units

questions.q: Slope of a line passing through $P ( 2, 3 )$ and intersecting the line $x + y = 7$ at a distance of $4$ units from $P,$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, the point& $P \left(2, 3\right)$~on the line~$x + y = 7 .$

Let, the point of~intersection of the two lines be~$Q$

Then, $Q$~can be taken as $Q ≡ ( \alpha,7 - \alpha )$

Given, $PQ = 4$~units and the distance between the points~ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ \text{ and } \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$~is~\sqrt{\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)2 + \left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)2}

$⇒ $\sqrt{( \alpha - {2 )}^{2} + \left(7 - \alpha - 3\right)2} =$4$

$⇒ $\sqrt{( \alpha - {2 )}^{2} + \left(4 - \alpha\right)2} =$4$

$⇒ ( \alpha - {2 )}^{2} + \left(4 - \alpha\right)2 = {4}^{2}$

$⇒ {α}^{2} - 4\alpha +4 + 16 - 8\alpha + {α}^{2} =16$

$⇒ 2{α}^{2} - 12\alpha +4 = 0$

$⇒ {α}^{2} - 6\alpha +2 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{- \left(- 6\right) \pm \sqrt{\left(- 6\right)2 - 4 \times 1 \times 2}}{2 \times 2}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 8}}{4}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{6 \pm 2\sqrt{7}}{4}$

$⇒ \alpha =3 \pm \sqrt{7}$

The slope of a line joining the points~ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ \text{ and } \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$~is~$\dfrac{{y}_{2} - {y}_{1}}{{x}_{2} - {x}_{1}} .$

If we take $\alpha =3 - \sqrt{7},$~then~$Q ≡ \left($3 - \sqrt{7},4 + \sqrt{7}\right)$

And, the slope of $PQ = m = \dfrac{4 + \sqrt{7} - 3}{3 - \sqrt{7} - 2} = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{7}}{1 - \sqrt{7}}$

If we take \alpha =$3 + \sqrt{7},$~then~$Q ≡ \left(3 + $\sqrt{7},$4 - $\sqrt{7}\right)

And, the slope of~$PQ = m = \dfrac{4 - \sqrt{7} - 3}{3 + \sqrt{7} - 2} = \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{7}}{1 + \sqrt{7}} .$

$

So,~$B ≡ \left(-a, 2a\right), C ≡ \left(5 + a, 2 + a\right)$

Now,~$B$~and~$C$~lies on the line~$x + py = 21a$, so

$- a + 2pa = 21a$

$⇒ p = 11$

Also,

$5 + a + 11\left(2 + a\right) = 21a$

$⇒ 27 = 9a ⇒ a = 3$

So,

$B ≡ \left(-$3, 6\right), C ≡ \left($8, 5\right)$

So,

$BC^{2} = 121 + 1 = 122

$

questions.q: Let $tan\alpha, tan\beta$ and $tan\gamma; \alpha, \beta, \gamma \ne \dfrac{( 2n - 1 ) \pi}{2}, n \in N$~be the slopes of the three line segments $OA, OB$~and $OC,$~respectively, where $O$ is origin. If circumcentre of $\Delta ABC$ coincides with origin and its orthocentre lies on $y$-axis, then the value of \left(\dfrac{cos3\alpha + cos3\beta + cos3\gamma}{cos\alpha \cdot cos\beta \cdot cos\gamma}\right)2$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, the slopes of the line segments& $OA, OB$~and~$OC$~are respectively,~$tan\alpha, tan\beta \text{ and } tan\gamma,$~then by parametric form the coordinates of the points~$A, B \text{ and } C$~can be taken respectively as~\left(OAcos\alpha, OAsin\alpha\right), \left(OBcos\beta, OBsin\beta\right) \text{ and } \left(OCcos\gamma, OCsin\gamma\right) .$

Given, the circumcentre of the~$∆ ABC$~is at origin and we know that the circumcentre is equidistant from the vertices of the triangle, hence~$OA = OB = OC .$

The centroid of a triangle with vertices~\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right), \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)~and~\left({x}_{3}, {y}_{3}\right)~is~\left(\dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + {x}_{3}}{3}, \dfrac{{y}_{1} + {y}_{2} + {y}_{3}}{3}\right),~thus the centroid of the~$∆ ABC$~is~\left(\dfrac{OA\left(∑ cos\alpha\right)}{3}, \dfrac{OA\left(∑ sin\alpha\right)}{3}\right) .

We know that for any triangle the circumcentre, orthocentre and centroid lie on a line.

Since, the orthocentre and circumcentre both lies on~$y$-axis, hence the centroid also lies on $y$-axis, hence the~$x$-coordinate of the centroid is zero.

$⇒ ∑ cos$\alpha =$0$

$⇒ cos$\alpha +$cos$\beta +$cos$\gamma =$0$

We know that, if~$a + b + c = 0,$~then~$a^{3} + b^{3} + c^{3} = 3abc,$

$⇒ \cos^{3}$\alpha + \cos^{3}\beta + \cos^{3}\gamma =$3 $\cdot$cos$\alpha \cdot$cos$\beta \cdot$cos$\gamma

Now, using~$cos3A = 4\cos^{3}A - 3cosA,$~we have

\left(\dfrac{cos3\alpha + cos3\beta + cos3\gamma}{cos\alpha \cdot cos\beta \cdot cos\gamma}\right)2 = \left(\dfrac{4\left(\cos^{3}\alpha + \cos^{3}\beta + \cos^{3}\gamma\right) - 3 ( cos\alpha + cos\beta + cos\gamma )}{cos\alpha \cdot cos\beta \cdot cos\gamma}\right)2$

$= \left(\dfrac{4\left(3 \cdot cos\alpha \cdot cos\beta \cdot cos\gamma\right) - 3 \left($0\right)}{cos\alpha \cdotcos\beta \cdotcos\gamma}\right)2$

$= \left(12\right)2 = 144 .$

$

questions.q: Let $A\left(\dfrac{3}{a}, \sqrt{a}\right), a > 0$, be a fixed point in the $xy$-plane. The image of $A$~in $y$-axis be $B$ and the image of $B$ in $x$-axis be $C$. If $D \left($3cos$\theta,$asin$\theta\right), ~is a point in the fourth quadrant such that the maximum area of $∆ ACD$~is $12$~square units, then $a \text{ and } is equal to _____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$A = \left(\dfrac{3}{a}, \sqrt{a}\right)$

$B = \$left(\dfrac{- 3}{a}, \sqrt{a}\right)$~is the image of~$A$~on y-axis

$C = \left(- $\dfrac{3}{a}, - \sqrt{a}\right)~is the image of~$B$~in x-axis

$D \lleft(3cos\theta,asin\theta\right)$

Area of triangle~$ACD$~will be

\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{a}$ \text{ and } $\sqrt{a}$ \text{ and } 1 \\ - $\dfrac{3}{a}$ \text{ and } - $\sqrt{a}$ \text{ and } 1 \\ 3cos\theta \text{ and } asin\theta \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right|$

$= $3\sqrt{a} \lleft($cos\theta --sin\theta\right)$

The maximum~area of triangle is~3\sqrt{a}\sqrt{2}

i.e.~3\sqrt{a}\sqrt{2} =$12$

$⇒ a = 8

$

questions.q: Consider a triangle having vertices $A ( - 2, 3 ) , B ( 1, 9 )$ and $C ( 3, 8 ) .$~If a line $L$ passing through the circum-centre of triangle $ABC,$~bisects line $BC,$~and intersects $y$-axis at point \left(0, \dfrac{α}{2}\right),$~then the value of real number $\alpha$ is _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$AB = \sqrt{\left(- 2 - 1\right)2 + \left(3 - 9\right)2} = \sqrt{45}$

$AC = \sqrt{\left(- 2 - 3\right)2 + \left(3 - 8\right)2} = \sqrt{50}$

$BC = \sqrt{\left(3 - 1\right)2 + \left(8 - 9\right)2} = \sqrt{5}$

Here,

$AC^{2} = AB^{2} + BC^{2}$

$⇒ ( \sqrt{50}{)}^{2} = ( \sqrt{45}{)}^{2} + ( \sqrt{5}{)}^{2}$

Hence,~$∠ B = 90 °$, so circumcentre is the mid-point of hypotenuse i.e.,~$AC$.

Circumcenter $≡ \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{11}{2}\right)$

Mid-point of $BC = \left($2, \dfrac{17}{2}\right)$

Equation of line~$L$~is

\left($y - \dfrac{11}{2}\right) = $\$left(\dfrac{\dfrac{11}{2} - \dfrac{17}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2} - 2}\right)\left($x - $\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$⇒ y = 2x + $\dfrac{9}{2}

Passing though \left(0, $\dfrac{α}{2}\right),so

\dfrac{α}{2} = \dfrac{9}{2}$⇒ \alpha =9$
